req.title: Sessions use secret key
req.statement: The system shall sign session cookies with the SECRET_KEY loaded from application config.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-034 requires that session cookies are signed with the SECRET_KEY from application config. We verify this by: (1) positive case — confirming that a valid session cookie is issued after login and is accepted on subsequent requests when the same SECRET_KEY is used; (2) negative case — confirming that a session cookie signed with a different SECRET_KEY is rejected (session data is not trusted, user is treated as anonymous); (3) boundary case — confirming that changing SECRET_KEY by even one character invalidates existing session cookies, catching constant-mutation operators. We also verify the exact SECRET_KEY value is used by the app config, and that the cookie header contains the 'session' cookie name.

tests.name: test_session_cookie_signed_with_correct_secret_key_positive
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a known SECRET_KEY
User 'Rahul' exists with password 'stone' in the pre-loaded database
actions: Capture the session cookie from the response
GET / with the session cookie to verify the session is accepted
expected: A 'session' cookie is present in the response headers
Subsequent GET / with the cookie returns HTTP 200
App config SECRET_KEY equals the value passed in test_config
trace: R-FLASKR-034: session cookies signed with SECRET_KEY from config
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
SECRET = 'test-secret-key-positive'
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': SECRET})
assert app.config['SECRET_KEY'] == SECRET

with app.test_client() as client:
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    cookies = r.headers.getlist('Set-Cookie')
    session_cookies = [c for c in cookies if c.startswith('session=')]
    assert len(session_cookies) == 1
    session_val = session_cookies[0]
    assert session_val.startswith('session=')
    r2 = client.get('/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_session_cookie_rejected_with_wrong_secret_key_negative
preconditions: Two app instances created with different SECRET_KEYs but same database
User 'Anjali' exists with password 'cloud' in the pre-loaded database
actions: Login with app_a (SECRET_KEY='key-alpha') to obtain a signed session cookie
Extract the raw session cookie value
Make a GET /create request to app_b (SECRET_KEY='key-beta') with the cookie from app_a
expected: GET /create on app_b with app_a's cookie returns HTTP 302 (redirect to login, not 200)
The session from app_a is not trusted by app_b due to different SECRET_KEY
trace: R-FLASKR-034: different SECRET_KEY must invalidate session cookies from other keys
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)

app_a = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'key-alpha'})
app_b = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'key-beta'})

assert app_a.config['SECRET_KEY'] == 'key-alpha'
assert app_b.config['SECRET_KEY'] == 'key-beta'
assert app_a.config['SECRET_KEY'] != app_b.config['SECRET_KEY']

with app_a.test_client() as client_a:
    r = client_a.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    cookies = r.headers.getlist('Set-Cookie')
    session_cookies = [c for c in cookies if c.startswith('session=')]
    assert len(session_cookies) == 1
    raw_cookie = session_cookies[0].split(';')[0]

with app_b.test_client() as client_b:
    client_b.set_cookie('session', raw_cookie.split('=', 1)[1])
    r2 = client_b.get('/create')
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    loc = r2.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert '/auth/login' in loc

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_session_cookie_invalidated_by_single_char_secret_key_change_boundary
preconditions: Two app instances: one with SECRET_KEY='boundary-secret-X', one with SECRET_KEY='boundary-secret-Y'
User 'Ishaan' exists with password 'stone' in the pre-loaded database
actions: Login with app_orig (SECRET_KEY='boundary-secret-X') to get a session cookie
Attempt to access /create which requires authentication
expected: GET /create on app_mutated with the cookie returns HTTP 302 to /auth/login
A single-character difference in SECRET_KEY is sufficient to invalidate the cookie
trace: R-FLASKR-034: boundary — even a 1-char change in SECRET_KEY must invalidate session
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)

KEY_ORIG = 'boundary-secret-X'
KEY_MUTATED = 'boundary-secret-Y'
assert KEY_ORIG != KEY_MUTATED
assert len(KEY_ORIG) == len(KEY_MUTATED)
assert KEY_ORIG[:-1] == KEY_MUTATED[:-1]

app_orig = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': KEY_ORIG})
app_mutated = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': KEY_MUTATED})

assert app_orig.config['SECRET_KEY'] == KEY_ORIG
assert app_mutated.config['SECRET_KEY'] == KEY_MUTATED

with app_orig.test_client() as c_orig:
    r = c_orig.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    cookies = r.headers.getlist('Set-Cookie')
    sess_cookies = [c for c in cookies if c.startswith('session=')]
    assert len(sess_cookies) == 1
    raw_val = sess_cookies[0].split(';')[0].split('=', 1)[1]

with app_mutated.test_client() as c_mut:
    c_mut.set_cookie('session', raw_val)
    r2 = c_mut.get('/create')
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    loc = r2.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert '/auth/login' in loc

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_default_secret_key_is_dev_and_overridable_state_transition
preconditions: App created without explicit SECRET_KEY uses default 'dev'
App created with explicit SECRET_KEY uses the provided value
actions: Create app with no SECRET_KEY override and check config
Create app with SECRET_KEY='production-secret' and check config
Verify the two configs differ and each matches its expected value
expected: The two SECRET_KEY values are not equal
trace: R-FLASKR-034: SECRET_KEY loaded from application config; default is 'dev'
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd1, path1 = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd1)
fd2, path2 = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd2)

app_default = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path1})
assert app_default.config['SECRET_KEY'] == 'dev'

app_override = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path2, 'SECRET_KEY': 'production-secret'})
assert app_override.config['SECRET_KEY'] == 'production-secret'
assert app_override.config['SECRET_KEY'] != 'dev'
assert app_default.config['SECRET_KEY'] != app_override.config['SECRET_KEY']

os.unlink(path1)
os.unlink(path2)

tests.name: test_session_cookie_same_secret_key_accepted_across_requests_decision_table
actions: Login as Diya to get session cookie
GET /create — should return 200 (session valid, user authenticated)
trace: R-FLASKR-034: same SECRET_KEY means session is consistently trusted across requests
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)

app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'consistent-key'})
assert app.config['SECRET_KEY'] == 'consistent-key'

with app.test_client() as client:
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Diya', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    cookies = r_login.headers.getlist('Set-Cookie')
    sess_cookies = [c for c in cookies if c.startswith('session=')]
    assert len(sess_cookies) == 1

    r_index = client.get('/')
    assert r_index.status_code == 200

    r_create = client.get('/create')
    assert r_create.status_code == 200

os.unlink(path)
